chain: Fewer sunspots and wrinkles over time
octinoxate.text: Octinoxate is a common UVB filter in sunscreens and SPF lip balms, used by skincare-minded people to keep skin looking younger and avoid sunburn and uneven tone. Its UVB absorption is well characterised; its appearance benefit comes through sun protection generally rather than trials of this filter alone.

chain: Fewer sunspots and wrinkles over time
oxybenzone.text: Oxybenzone is a broad-spectrum sunscreen filter used in sunscreens and lip products so skin stays smoother and more even-toned in the sun. The anti-aging case rests on sunscreen-class evidence for UV protection, not on studies of oxybenzone's own effect on appearance.

octisalate.text: Octisalate is a mild UVB filter added to sunscreens to lift SPF and keep filters like avobenzone stable, so daily sunscreen can protect skin from photoaging. It is also an emollient that adds water resistance. Evidence is for sunscreen formulas as a class, not octisalate alone.

homosalate.text: Homosalate is a common UVB filter in sunscreens, used for daily protection that helps keep skin looking even-toned and younger. Its appearance benefit is inferred from sunscreen-class evidence on UV damage rather than studies of homosalate specifically.

ensulizole.text: Ensulizole is used in light, non-greasy facial lotions and daily moisturisers, so people can wear sun protection under makeup every day and slow sun-driven skin aging. Evidence is sunscreen-class, not specific to appearance outcomes of this filter.

ecamsule.text: Ecamsule (Mexoryl SX) is a photostable UVA filter prized in European and Asian sunscreens by users wanting protection against the UVA rays linked to wrinkling and pigmentation. Its use in sunscreens is established; appearance outcomes are inferred from UVA protection in general.

bemotrizinol.text: Bemotrizinol (Tinosorb S) is a favourite among skincare enthusiasts for broad-spectrum, photostable sunscreens, often sought from EU, Australian and Asian products to protect skin from aging UV. Evidence is from sunscreen testing and long regional use rather than appearance trials.

chain: Particle filter covers UVA and UVB
bisoctrizole.text: Bisoctrizole (Tinosorb M) is a hybrid particulate filter in sunscreens abroad, sought by users wanting broad UVA and UVB coverage to protect skin from photoaging. Evidence is sunscreen-class and formulation-based; appearance outcomes of this filter alone are not studied.

diethylamino-hydroxybenzoyl-hexyl-benzoa.text: DHHB (Uvinul A Plus) is a photostable UVA filter common in non-US sunscreens, valued by skincare users for protection against the UVA rays tied to wrinkles and dark spots. Support is lab and regulatory data, not trials of appearance.

ethylhexyl-triazone.text: Ethylhexyl triazone is a highly photostable UVB filter used in high-SPF sunscreens abroad, so people can reach strong protection that preserves skin tone and youthfulness. No clinical trials of it alone exist; the link to appearance comes from sunscreen use generally.

drometrizole-trisiloxane.text: Drometrizole trisiloxane (Mexoryl XL) is a photostable filter in L'Oreal-brand sunscreens and daily-wear skincare, often paired with ecamsule, used by people seeking everyday protection against skin aging. Evidence is formulation and regulatory data, not appearance trials.

enzacamene.text: Enzacamene (4-MBC) is an older camphor-derived UVB filter that appeared in sunscreens, where the aim was protecting skin from sun aging. It is now banned in EU cosmetics, so it mainly comes up in ingredient-checking discussions. Appearance outcomes were not studied for it specifically.

amiloxate.text: Amiloxate is a cinnamate UVB filter found in EU sunscreens, used for general sun protection that helps skin stay even and youthful. Its appearance benefit is inferred from sunscreen-class evidence; beyond photoallergy case reports, little specific to it is studied.

bisdisulizole-disodium.text: Bisdisulizole disodium (Neo Heliopan AP) is a water-soluble UVA filter in EU sunscreens, used in light textures that suit daily facial wear and protect against UVA-linked wrinkles and dark spots. Evidence is regulatory and formulation-based, not appearance trials.

meradimate.text: Meradimate is an older anthranilate UVA filter listed in US sunscreen rules, used to add some UVA coverage that helps protect skin from sun aging. It has been studied mostly for its photophysics rather than for appearance outcomes.

padimate-o.text: Padimate O is an older PABA-derived UVB filter once common in sunscreens and lip products, used to protect skin from sun damage. It is rarely used now and appears mostly in ingredient history discussions; appearance outcomes were not studied for it specifically.

paba.text: PABA was one of the first sunscreen actives, used for decades to prevent burning and sun-aged skin, and is now known in appearance culture mainly as the ingredient modern formulas moved away from. Its UVB absorption is well established; long-term appearance trials of PABA are not.

cinoxate.text: Cinoxate is an older cinnamate UVB filter, US-approved in 1961, that appeared in some sunscreens to protect skin from sun damage. It is rarely used now and appears mainly in ingredient lists and history; its appearance effect was not studied separately.

dioxybenzone.text: Dioxybenzone (benzophenone-8) is a sunscreen filter in the US monograph, used to add UVB and short-UVA coverage that protects skin from sun aging. It has almost no dedicated research, so its appearance benefit is inferred from sunscreen-class evidence.

chain: Less UV damage to skin and hair
sulisobenzone.text: Sulisobenzone (benzophenone-4) is a water-soluble UV filter in some sunscreens and in hair products meant to protect colour and structure. People use such products for sun protection of skin and dyed hair. Research on it is mostly environmental, not appearance-focused.

chain: Mild sun-filter role in old products
trolamine-salicylate.text: Trolamine salicylate is best known as the active in odourless muscle-pain creams, and was historically used as a weak UVB absorber in sunscreens and cosmetics. Its appearance link is minor and rarely drawn today; its sunscreen role rests on older formulation use rather than appearance studies.

chain: Less UV damage to skin and lips
polysilicone-15.text: Polysilicone-15 (Parsol SLX) is a UVB filter used in EU sunscreens, lip balms and hair products, so users can protect skin, lips and colour-treated hair from sun. Evidence consists of formulation data and case-report safety data, not appearance trials.

chain: Broad UV protection in daily wear
tris-biphenyl-triazine.text: Tris-biphenyl triazine (Tinosorb A2B) is a newer particulate filter that skincare enthusiasts look for in daily-wear sunscreens for broad UV coverage against skin aging. Only lab and formulation research exists, with no human trials of its effect on appearance.

methoxypropylamino-cyclohexenylidene-eth.text: This L'Oreal filter (Mexoryl 400, UVMune) targets long-wave UVA1, the range tied to wrinkling and pigmentation, and is promoted in La Roche-Posay sunscreens. It gained EU approval in 2019; no published human trials show appearance outcomes.

chain: Absorbs UVB, UVA and blue light
phenylene-bis-diphenyltriazine.text: Phenylene bis-diphenyltriazine (TriAsorB) is a newer filter its developers say covers UV and high-energy blue light, which appeals to users worried about sun-driven pigmentation and aging. The evidence is mostly developer-authored; independent appearance data are not available.

chain: Mineral filter reflects and absorbs UV
titanium-dioxide.text: Titanium dioxide is the classic mineral sunscreen filter and white pigment, used in physical sunscreens and tinted SPF to protect skin from sun aging and even out tone for the day. Sunscreen protection is well established; it is weaker on long UVA.

chain: Mineral filter blocks UVA and UVB
zinc-oxide.text: Zinc oxide is a broad-spectrum mineral sunscreen filter used by people seeking gentle, photostable protection that preserves youthful, even skin. It also forms the base of barrier creams. The UV protection is well established; appearance benefit follows from reduced photoaging.

nano-zinc-oxide.text: Nano zinc oxide is the transparent version of the mineral filter, used so mineral sunscreens go on without a white cast while still protecting skin from sun aging. The sheer finish is directly visible; the debate is about penetration and aquatic toxicity.

nano-titanium-dioxide.text: Nano titanium dioxide is used in modern mineral sunscreens so they look sheer rather than chalky, which makes daily wear easier and supports protection against sun aging. Protection is well established for the category; the nano-specific safety debate continues.

cerium-oxide.text: Cerium oxide is discussed as a possible mineral UV absorber with lower photocatalytic activity than zinc oxide or titanium dioxide, which would suit sunscreens aimed at preventing skin aging. Antioxidant nanoceria research exists; sunscreen evidence for appearance does not.
